newsitem.title: USA: No luck for Arkansas gambling amendment.
newsitem.headline: No luck for Arkansas gambling amendment.

text.p: Arkansas voters defeated a gambling proposal called Amendment 4 by what appears to be a 64 percent margin, according to the executive director of a committee that opposed the measure.
According to Larry Page, executive director of the Christian Civic Action Committee, early results show 271,880 million voters opposed the measure, while 174,174 voters favored it.
"If my calculator was true to me this morning, that's 64 percent," Page said. "It didn't say how many precincts, that's got to be most, but it's not all obviously."
Once the official results are in, the margin of defeat will probably won't change by much, he said.
"I think it's clear to say we are going to have 60 percent plus," Page said.
Amemdment 4 would have established a state lottery, permitted charitable bingo and raffles, and would have allowed local voters in Hot Springs to decide whether they wanted three casinos.

Arkansans' defeat of the measure was particularly notable considering the amount of money proponents of various gambling measures spent, Page said. Though Amendment 4 was the only gambling proposal to see election day, three other amendments had been the proposed. The Arkansas State Supreme Court, however, struck them due to ballot title problems.

Page said supporters of those four amemdments will probably end up having spent $9 million to $10 million in their failed attempt, with Amendment 4 backers probably having spent $6 million to $7 million of that alone.
"Contrast that with $400 million spent by us," he said.
